content.title: About
content.content: Condensed sweetened milk is a thick milk product made by evaporating whole milk and adding sugar. It has a sweet, caramel-like flavor and a creamy texture, commonly used in desserts, beverages, and confectionery.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Condensed milk was invented in the 19th century as a way to preserve milk without refrigeration.
Sweetened condensed milk is a key ingredient in traditional dishes worldwide, such as Brazilian brigadeiro or Indian kulfi.
During evaporation, lactose concentration increases, enhancing the product’s sweetness.
It can replace fresh milk in recipes that require a thick consistency.
Some markets offer unsweetened versions, usually labeled as "unsweetened".

items.title: Calcium source
items.content: Condensed milk provides calcium, essential for bone and teeth health.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: It contains vitamins B2 and B12, supporting energy metabolism.

items.title: Energy dense
items.content: High sugar and fat content offers a quick source of energy.

items.title: Protein
items.content: Milk protein contributes to tissue building and repair.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: Small amounts of phosphorus and magnesium support various bodily functions.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: Excessive intake may lead to weight gain and increase diabetes risk.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: People with lactose intolerance may experience discomfort after consumption.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: Individuals allergic to milk proteins can have allergic reactions.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Condensed milk is very calorie‑dense, so portion control is important.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Use condensed milk in baking, for making custards, toppings, in coffee, ice cream, or as a sweet filling for pancakes and waffles. It can be stirred into hot tea or blended into milkshakes.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the unopened can in a cool, dry place. Once opened, keep it refrigerated and consume within 1‑2 weeks. Discard if it develops off‑flavors, discoloration, or signs of fermentation.
